description: A CONSOLE RUN is an Agent SDK NATIVE RUNNER that Chief OBSERVES, not a scheduler inside Chief (docs/decisions/native-harness-observer-first.md). A generic runner on the Claude Agent SDK, modelled on ~/insimul-loops/briefs/console_plan_run.py, drives map -> synthesize -> plan -> gauntlet <-> revise -> final (and optionally execute) over one or more repos, billed to a Claude Console organization's API credits (the promotional credit covers the Agent SDK and the API, not Claude Code). Agents return documents and the runner writes every phase to a file you can read, correct and rerun; it emits one chief.loop-run/v1 manifest per run, validated by collectors/gauntlet/validate_observation.py, which Chief's collectors read like any other observation. `chief console` is a compatibility launcher for the runner (like `chief run`); it never owns the loop. Design: docs/explanation/console-runs.md; prompts: templates/console/. Execute mode builds on a branch in a worktree and never merges.

userStories.title: `chief console --dry-run` prints every phase's prompt and SDK options and calls nothing
userStories.description: The runner (apps/console-run/) and its compatibility launcher, with no model call and no SDK import needed.
acceptanceCriteria: `bin/chief console <repo>... --brief <file> --dry-run` starts the runner, which fills each template under templates/console/ (every {{NAME}} from its README's table) and prints, per phase, the prompt and the exact ClaudeAgentOptions it would pass (model, allowed_tools, permission_mode, max_turns, cwd, add_dirs) and the phase's dollar cap, without importing or calling the SDK.
A template left with an unfilled `{{` makes the run exit non-zero naming the placeholder (test/console-dry-run.sh).
README's command table and docs/reference list the command as a compatibility launcher for a native runner; the docs gate passes.

userStories.title: The credential never reaches a shell environment
userStories.description: Billing to the Console organization without exporting ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
acceptanceCriteria: The runner authenticates through CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (default ~/.chief/claude-console, a Console sign-in) set only on the SDK process, or a key read from the macOS Keychain and passed only in the env the runner hands the SDK; `chief console --check` reports which credential source is active without printing any secret.

A test proves the parent shell's environment is unchanged after a run, that no *_API_KEY variable is set in the launcher's own process, and that no key appears in run.json, cost.jsonl, log.txt or loop-run.json (test/console-credential.sh).

userStories.title: Plan mode runs end to end on a fixture repo with a stub SDK
userStories.description: The phases, the run record and resumption, without spending credits.
acceptanceCriteria: Against a fixture repo and a stub Agent SDK module (same query()/ClaudeAgentOptions/ResultMessage surface) that answers each phase from canned files, `--mode plan` writes <run-dir>/ with brief.md, run.json, log.txt, map/*.md, architecture.md, plan.md, roadmap.json, critic/<lens>-r<n>.json, decisions.md, final/ and cost.jsonl; the agents only return text and the runner writes every file.
The gauntlet loop stops when every lens returns pass with no blocker or major, or at the round cap; an unparseable verdict becomes one major finding.

A phase whose file exists is reused on rerun; `--to map` stops after the mappers; a brief's own lens file is added as a lens; a call whose cap would push the total over the budget is not made and the run says so.

userStories.title: Final output generates valid tasklists
userStories.description: The plan becomes Chief work through the existing generator.
acceptanceCriteria: The runner runs `chief gen -n` on final/roadmap.json and records the result in final/chief-gen-check.txt; a fixture roadmap that fails is reported with the failing items.

userStories.title: The run emits a valid chief.loop-run/v1 manifest and an observer finds it
userStories.description: Chief observes the run through the gauntlet observation contract.
acceptanceCriteria: Every run (finished, stopped or paused) writes <run-dir>/loop-run.json: one chief.loop-run/v1 with one lane whose stages are map, synthesize, plan, gauntlet, revise, final (and execute in execute mode); each lens round is a chief.round/v1, each critic finding a chief.finding/v1, each SDK call a chief.native-session/v1 (provider claude, attribution provider-api, externalId = the result's session_id; cost, session_id and tokens under extensions["anthropic.agent-sdk"]), and each phase file a chief.evidence/v1 with its sha256.

The manifest passes collectors/gauntlet/validate_observation.py before it is written, and nothing is written if it fails; a stub call that fails with a credit-exhausted error leaves the run, lane and stage `paused` with the reason in runtime.pauseReasons.

A test points the portfolio collector's `loopRuns` setting at the fixture run's manifest and finds the run in the snapshot's loopRuns with its status and lane (test/console-observed.sh); Chief's collectors are read, not changed.

userStories.title: Execute mode builds one tasklist through the SDK in a worktree and never merges
userStories.description: Building through the Agent SDK in a worktree, bounded like the loops.
acceptanceCriteria: `--mode execute --tasklist NN` runs builder then critic rounds (stop: zero blocker and zero major, at most 5 rounds); the builder is an SDK call with cwd = its own git worktree, permission_mode acceptEdits and a scoped allowed_tools; the critic is read-only with fresh context; with the stub SDK a fixture tasklist reaches pass in round 2 and its rounds appear in the manifest's execute stage.

Heavy commands are wrapped by `--lock <cmd>` when given; no base branch is ever written (asserted in the test); the branch is left for the operator or `chief run`'s merge phase; the worktree is removed when the run ends.

userStories.title: Spend is recorded and capped
userStories.description: Cost per call from the SDK result message.
acceptanceCriteria: cost.jsonl records label, model, session_id, usd, tokens and seconds per call from the SDK's ResultMessage; the same figures appear on the call's native session in the manifest; a run's total never exceeds the budget in the stub test.
